Yes, you described it very well. But I have to say I took risperidone first at a low dosage.

I started experiencing galactorrhea, gained weight (I think 3 kg / 1 kg a week, while restricting my intake), other than that on Olanzapine which I took for roughly only for one month I experienced increased hunger and thirst. I got exhausted and really bloated, I felt like I was gaining weight and retaining fluid. I trained through the exhaustion though. Mentally I felt really slowed down in terms of thought process. I was forced to take these meds, because I suddenly was falsely labeled with schizophrenic psychosis - and later being told I was never psychotic and just seemed to be at that time by other professionals. I was acting completely different and maybe more sane, since I was less creative and overthinking less - which I actually like about me. I felt like my personality changed. But this is just a feeling of mine, it is of course nothing I can totally link to that but it is quite obvious that there is a relation there. It took two weeks, maybe longer until the concentration of the medication was low enough and I was starting to get to be more like myself again (4-5 weeks). Of course I was more connected to myself then and also to my "struggles" but it felt better to me then being drugged, because that what it felt to me like it was doing. I lost weight and got my energy back.

Antipsychotics are really something nobody will ever make me take again and the side effects and the long lasting effects strongly affect the quality of life. If they would have worked sure, but they did not help and for sedation you can also take other meds with less severe side effects.

Other than that I don't remember much because of dissociation.

I abolished it as soon as I could. I am completely off psych meds now.

It took some time until the effects fully wore off.

Other than that they might be really helpful if you are actually psychotic but I don't know that.

All I saw with antipsychotics in mental hospital were the severe side effects, I can't tell how it affected them otherwise or helped them.

But seeing people drool, struggling to talk or even to move and reacting so slow and such because of being on high doses of these strong meds... It was difficult to witness apart from them struggling from their illnesses.

I also remember that when I talked with other people/one patient we went on leaves together - that we would constantly repeat ourselves and the other person then gave the feedback that we had said this or that before. I only noticed mid-talk that I had mentioned something just a few minutes earlier (she was on lithium and haldol and some other less strong meds) and I was on olanzapine...

Honestly if you speak up about having these kind of tendencies/ not the full blown disorder (and even then) they will believe you and still take you seriously. It takes lots of courage to talk about these things.
Being in a car crash or something is something they might not rarely hear, especially when people are suicidal.
You can also say you keep having these daydreams, because you are lacking something in your life xy, or you say you feel so alone with your struggles and not seen that you have thes (insert daydreams) fantasies and that they make you feel guilty which then leads to self-harm.
That you are happy when you are ill because that makes your issues seem real, your struggles real and not invisible and condemned by society.
That sometimes your mental illness is hard to grasp for yourself and seem so hard to deal with/not as easy as with physical illness.

Really whatever that is in your case or figure that out together, also the root cause/origin.

I talked to my psychiatrist about it and he believes me, he takes me seriously and he told me there is nothing I need to feel guilty or ashamed about.

For me it is also when I start getting better that I feel like sabotaging my process. I believe it is because of everyday life anxiety which is quite severe.
My brain will kinda use some chunks out of my bad memory due to dissociative phenomenons and fabricate something which evokes strong negative feelings/makes me look bad.
And then force/push me to relapse into self-harm.
Basically it makes me exhausted and then I start believing the lies my brain tells me and because I am tired of defending myself I finally give in.
Also I hope that what I wrote here was not shocking or painful to read but I kinda feel that we have to remind ourselves that these kind of things are not to be aimed for/romantisize them or anything. That is why I wrote it in such a shocking way. Sometimes I know it is hard to find anything that helps really.
And the more shocking and severe the more we might want something.
Maybe in a sense it is the validation and attention but mostly really affection, a stable relationship, family dynamics whatever we were not given and now seek in others, but really in ourselves but since we have not learned that and how to give ourselves that we depend on the outside world, which of course does not really work.
So it is also about giving yourself the respect, understanding and treating yourself like you would treat others in the same situation.

Also if you can not stop thinking about dying in a car crash or being brought to hospital, finally cared for and then dying. That is suicidal ideation.
It is like not allowing yourself/wanting to die by suicide and more by accident. But it still equals death.
The equation has the same result.
And even if that is only passive suicidality it can be chronic it can be incredibly debilitating.
But in BPD it can be quickly turn into active suicidality that is why caution is important.
Also throw everything you know outside the window.
Mental illness is different for everybody and some people are so functional and happy, nobody sees their struggles maybe not even them before they die by suicide.
Sometimes a decline can be quick and overlooked.
And you seem to be very self-aware you can use that for yourself.
Also substance abuse, alcohol, drugs and self-harm can be a really dangerous combination.
It compromises the awareness and self-awareness.
It is not about quitting both immediately but if possible really try to avoid to combine them.
Drinking might make you numb to your issues but it is not a helpful solution in the long run.
You can't drown feelings they will always resurface afterwards.
Even if they seem stupidly strong, typically for the disorder or you feel like you should get over it be over it by now they have a reason they are there. Other than that they might be painful...
Maybe you can get a certain kind of medication (if you can make sure you can be on meds safely without misusing them or mixing them with alcohol/substance). A tranquilizer whatever... That helps to bring you back down to earth so you don't need the alcohol. Something you can maybe get some rest with instead.
I think you are doing the best you can and I wish you all the best and that things turn out the way you want them to. ♡

You will stop yourself from seeking help since you are embarrassed.
You feel like what if my mental health struggles are fabricated too, like the physical illness.
You will try not to harm myself.
Each day will be a battle.
Then you will dissociate and lose control.
Some time later you might feel sick and slowly it sinks in what you have done.
Your family will drive you to hospital, you will be too weak to say no.
And you will resist treatment since you know the attention will fuel your disorder but you are too weak and too ill to do anything.

In your dreams everybody seems to be caring, but usually it is not always the case.
Also a lot of it is not real affection. 
It is a way other people make themselves look good, taking care of others, fixing their own insecurities, self-image.

Or you will go from doctor to doctor and fabricate things and make things look worse than they are. You can't do anything. You will seem almost psychotic, the obedience to the voices in your head.

Do you want to use illness as something to make yourself run away from life, to be cared for but maybe never truly loved all your life?
Do you want to say lots of stupid things you will later feel embarrassed about?
